text:
Predicates:
BornWithSiblings(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth with siblings.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
ComplainsAboutSiblings(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home.
LiveWithStrangers(x) ::: x lives with strangers.
Luke ::: the individual named Luke.
Premises:
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → BornWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time with siblings, then they were born in a multiple birth.
∀x (ComplainsAboutSiblings(x) → ∃y (BornWithSiblings(y) ∧ Siblings(x,y))) ::: If people complain about siblings, then they have siblings born together.
∀x (LiveAtHome(x) → ¬LiveWithStrangers(x)) ::: If people live at home, then they do not live with strangers.
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend time with siblings, then they often live at home.
LukeBornMultiple :: Luke is either born in a multiple birth and lives with strangers, or not born in a multiple birth and does not live with strangers.
Conclusion:
¬(BornWithSiblings(Luke)) ∧ ¬(ComplainsAboutSiblings(Luke)) ::: Luke is neither born in a multiple birth nor complains often about annoying siblings.
